chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Umar ibn Muslim, from al-Hasan ibn Uqbah ibn al-Nahmi, from Abu Ishaq al-Banna, from Jabir al-Ja'fi who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The Qaim will receive allegiance between the Rukn and the Maqam by three hundred and thirteen, the number of the people of Badr. Among them are the nobles from Egypt, the Abdal from Syria, and the virtuous from Iraq. He will remain in power for as long as Allah wills.

key_terms.أَهْلُ بَدْرٍ: The people of Badr, referring to the 313 companions of the Prophet at the Battle of Badr
key_terms.الرُّكْنُ: The Rukn, a specific pillar of the Kaaba
key_terms.الْأَبْدَالُ: The Abdal, a term for righteous substitutes or spiritual leaders
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Qaim (The Riser), a title for Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.)
key_terms.وَالْمَقَامُ: And the Maqam, the station of Prophet Ibrahim (a.s.) near the Kaaba

ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics and number of the initial companions of Imam al-Mahdi (aj) according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* outlines the eschatological rise of Imam al-Mahdi (aj), emphasizing the symbolic number of 313 companions to mirror the faithful at Badr, thereby linking the Mahdi’s movement to the foundational victory of Islam. It highlights the geographical diversity of the elite companions—specifically the 'Nujaba' from Egypt, 'Abdal' from Syria, and 'Akhbar' from Iraq—signifying a global coalition of righteous supporters. The narration concludes by affirming that the duration of his rule is divinely decreed, underscoring the certainty of his eventual establishment of justice.
